newsitem.title: UK: UK gilts end lower after strong retail sales.
newsitem.headline: UK gilts end lower after strong retail sales.

text.p: UK gilts ended 19/32 lower on Wednesday, dragged down by higher-than-expected May retail sales data.
"Gilts were pushed down low this morning, but the main move has been short sterling. People have been revising their interest-rate expectations," said GNI senior trader Mark Henry.
Retail sales rose 1.1 percent in the month of May against an expectations of a 0.2 percent rise. Growth rates for three and 12 months reached levels last seen in the consumer boom of 1988.
"The key issue that's come up today is that the monetary policy committee is likely to tighten by 25 basis points at its next meeting on the back of the retail sales figure," Henry said.
The September gilt futures contract closed 19/32 lower at 113-15/32, barely off the day's low of 113-12/32.
The market remained cautious ahead of Thursday's M4 broad money data, with traders expecting a strong M4 figure on the back of the strong retail sales data, Henry said.
The Reuters consensus forecast suggests M4 rose 0.7 percent in May for year-on-year growth of 10.0 percent.
"But I think the market is beginning to accept the likelihood of a quarter point rate rise," Henry added.
The National Audit Office is on Thursday due to release a review of former Chancellor Kenneth Clark's budget assumptions.
"The feeling is Brown will use the report as an excuse to tighten quite agressively on the fiscal side, which would be very good for gilts," Henry said.
Brown will deliver his first budget on July 2. Financial markets are forecasting fiscal tightening of around 3.0 billion stg, with any tax rises likely to be directed at the corporate sector.

The spread between gilts and Bunds at 10 years widened to 154 basis points, the widest since Brown announced the Bank of England's independence to set interest rates. It stood at 145 basis points on Wednesday.
The short sterling strip edged down after the strong retail sales data and all contracts lost ground.
September short sterling settled at 93.06, down 10 basis points, comfortably factoring in a quarter point rate rise by the end of the third quarter and flirting with a half point rise.
December lost 11 basis points to close at 92.88.
